ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, the horizontal axis is “latitude value of the direct solar point,” from 0° to 23.5°; the vertical axis is “sunrise time (hour),” from 0 o'clock to 6 o'clock. The four curves ①②③④ all start from sunrise at about 6 o'clock when the direct solar point is 0°. As the latitude value of the direct solar point increases, the sunrise times represented by the four curves all become earlier, but by different magnitudes: curve ① changes the least, only slowly dropping from 6 o'clock to a little more than about 5 o'clock; curve ② drops relatively obviously, approaching 0 o'clock near 23.5°; curves ③ and ④ drop faster, approaching 0 o'clock earlier. Then reason: Hangzhou City, Zhejiang Province is approximately located at 30°N, belonging to the middle-low latitude region, and has no polar day phenomenon. At the spring and autumn equinoxes, sunrise is about 6 o'clock; around the summer solstice, the day length becomes longer and sunrise will be earlier, but generally it is around 5 o'clock and will not be earlier to 0 o'clock. Therefore, the curve corresponding to Hangzhou should be the curve whose sunrise time changes relatively little, dropping from 6 o'clock to a little more than about 5 o'clock. The one in the figure that fits this feature is curve ①.
